context.title: Load baseline context
context.imperative: Read your inherited global doctrine (this skill's references/global-orchestrator.md and references/global-everyone.md), then the project deltas: docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md, docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md, docs/agents/engine-config.json. Where the repo carries no docs/agents/ overlay at all (e.g. a skill-source repo), substitute the closest repo doctrine you can find (README, CONTRIBUTING, top-level docs) and record the substitution — do not treat those paths as guaranteed to exist. Before you open any source file, resolve and read the map input: run py /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/map_orient.py orient --root /home/tommy/projects/constellation-skills-wt/epic-568-315 --work-id commander-315. On RESOLVED, read the entrypoint it names and the packets, overlays and decision anchors it routes you to for the area the ask touches, and treat every later source read as confirming a frame the map already gave you rather than building one out of code. On DEGRADED, re-run the same command with --substitute PATH (what you read instead of a map — it is hash-pinned into the receipt) --unmapped TEXT (what stayed unmapped) --escalation TEXT (what you are escalating, and to whom), and get that on the record before any source read: degraded is a declared reading, never a licence to start from code. The tool probes a fixed fallback order — README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, a docs/ index — and labels a substitute it found there as verified by the filesystem rather than merely asserted by you. The anchor of this instruction is the point: 'before you open any source file' is an act you cannot postpone, whereas a map-first imperative anchored to a late artifact (the gate plan, which is authored at the END of a long run) is satisfied by a run that crawls source for fifty calls, reads the map afterwards, and has complied exactly — that is measured behaviour, not a hypothetical. This read is the map-first input the mission frame and plan are built from. Attest c1.

postconditions.statement: orchestrator context, glossary, engine config loaded; current map read for the affected area where architecture artifacts exist

the orientation contract is satisfied -- RESOLVED, or a DEGRADED verdict discharged with hash-pinned substitutes AND the unmapped gap AND an escalation -- recorded at the context step, which precedes understand and plan. Ordering itself is NOT machine-verifiable from a receipt: nothing in a receipt distinguishes a run that resolved the map first from one that crawled fifty files and then wrote an identical receipt. Ordering lives in this step's imperative ('Before you open any source file') and in the report-only ordering audit, never in this check. This gate is a regression floor so map-IGNORING cannot silently return; it is NOT the fix for map-LATENESS (measured sensitivity 0/4, specificity 0/1). Gate-vs-report is a flag flip: adding --report-only to 'py /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/map_orient.py verify-orientation --root /home/tommy/projects/constellation-skills-wt/epic-568-315 --work-id commander-315' turns this gate into a non-blocking report without rewiring the step.

plan.title: Author the gate plan
plan.imperative: Map-first: BEFORE authoring execute.json, produce a mission frame from the map input the context step resolved, using templates/MISSION_FRAME.template.md (intent; affected capabilities; relevant examples/events; structural anchors; governing constraints/assumptions; decision anchors and decision pressure; claims/evidence surfaces; map confidence/staleness/disputes; out of scope). Write it to .agent-work/commander-315/MISSION_FRAME.md — that exact path is what the c6 gate reads, so a frame parked anywhere else reads as no frame at all. For a trivial local/mechanical change where the map adds nothing, shrink or skip the frame and say so in its intent; c6 is waivable, so take that escape as a RECORDED waiver (<engine> waive plan --cond c6 --authority human --reason '...') rather than as a silent skip. The c6 gate runs map_orient.py verify-frame over that file: every anchor id the frame cites must exist in the map inventory the context step resolved, or — when context came back DEGRADED — must be one of the substitutes the receipt hash-pinned there, so the frame is compared against a committed prior declaration instead of a same-breath assertion. Know what that check is and is not, and do not overclaim it: it is a regression floor so map-IGNORING cannot silently return, not the fix for map-LATENESS. Measured against this epic's baseline five runs it has sensitivity 0/4 and specificity 0/1, and it inherits the late-anchor defect it was built next to, because anchors-in-a-late-frame is compliance without sequence. The load-bearing map-first anchor is at the context step ('before you open any source file'), which is why verify-orientation is gated there and verify-frame is gated only here. Do NOT 'fix' that asymmetry by also running verify-frame at context: no frame exists at context — the step runs before understand and plan — and the only way to make it pass there is to let an ABSENT frame pass, which is exactly the refusal the whole check is built on. If verify-frame ever has to be context-safe, give it a step-scoped mode; never a vacuous pass. For any low-confidence/stale/disputed map area the run depends on, alter the plan accordingly: add a scout/verification gate or surface it to the human as a decision — never author gates that silently trust an unverified map. Surface durable-structure choices as decision candidates per the skill's Decision candidates section rather than choosing alone. Then author the gate plan into execute.json: each gate the smallest reasonable bite, with close criteria, required evidence, and an anchors block cut from the frame. Before the plan-approved checkpoint run plan-alternatives (parallel gate-plan candidates under distinct constraints, via the references/design-it-twice-brief.md contract) and a cold plan critic (reads the candidate plan + mission frame only, no authoring context); both bias-to-yes — any skip is surfaced as a named untaken road — and the panel-vs-single choice is surfaced to the human at plan approval. Get the human to approve it. In delegated mode, satisfy c3 (plan approved) by attaching a user-decision evidence item citing the launch order's frozen plan and scope -- by default via the spine_evidence MCP tool (action=attach, task_id=plan, evidence_type=user-decision, fields={cite: 'LAUNCH_ORDER:Mission'}); CLI fallback: attach plan --type user-decision --field cite='LAUNCH_ORDER:Mission'; surface a plan-invalidating discovery to the Admiral rather than blocking on the human. See the commander skill's Delegated/autonomous mode.

execute.context_headroom_note: #467. Absolute-token context reserve for THIS gate only: the engine subtracts it from both the soft and hard caps before dividing by the model's window, so `execute` may not be BEGUN with less than this much room left below the hard cap. It makes the imperative's existing prose instruction ('ensure context headroom before entering') enforceable, and it can only ever tighten -- no gate can raise a threshold. WHY 30000, and it is a GUESS, revisable in place: `execute` is the run's longest gate and the one that cannot be abandoned halfway, because it drives every crew gate and each crew dispatch costs tens of thousands of tokens. The only observation available was a commander sitting at ~127K fill after a cold resume plus one full three-task gate -- which bounds one gate's marginal cost in the tens of thousands but cannot separate it from the resume baseline. 30K is a round number at the low end of that range: on claude-opus-5 (1M window, 80K soft / 150K hard) it moves execute's begin-work line from 15% to 12% and its advisory from 8% to 5%, while every other gate keeps the shipped default. The named settle experiment (read fill_fraction across completed commander runs at the moment execute was started) is NOT runnable from existing artifacts -- gauge.json keeps only the latest reading and the per-gate context manifests record no fill -- so a later run may revise this number here, in this one place, without re-deriving anything.

feedback.title: Record workflow feedback
feedback.imperative: Before committing, reflect honestly on how this run actually went: how closely you followed the skills, handoffs, and checklists; where you had to improvise or work around the instructions; what was ambiguous, missing, or contradictory; and what would have helped. Include the crew Workflow Feedback harvested at each gN-integrate. A 'none' answer requires a run-specific reason ('none — confirmed after review: <what you checked>'); a bare 'none' does not close this step. Then record what happened as EPISODES: one episode per distinct thing that happened — not one per run, and not a summary — each stating its task-intent, expected-behavior, observed-behavior, impact-cost and workaround. An episode is a record, not a rule: write what you observed, and do NOT write a rule for a future agent to follow — a rule to follow belongs in docs/agents/* and is a human's call. Write the delta to .agent-work/commander-315/episode-delta.json and apply it deterministically: py /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/apply_episode_delta.py --delta .agent-work/commander-315/episode-delta.json --store-root episodes. Pass --store-root on every invocation: the writer's default resolves relative to the installed skill directory, so an installed copy would silently build a store at ~/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/episodes — outside the repo — while every gate reported green. Never hand-edit a file under episodes/: that writer is the only write path into it. Then run the capture gate before advancing: py /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/verify_episode_captured.py commander-315 --store-root episodes --phase feedback.

postconditions.statement: this run captured at least one episode: an episode in the store records this work id

archive.title: Archive, commit, and push
archive.imperative: Commit all remaining work, including this run's episodes under episodes/. That is a tracked repo-root path, so the committed episode IS the durable record: it survives `git worktree remove` and lands in a fresh clone. None of the old is-.agent-work-gitignored reasoning applies to it. Push the branch to remote. When you open a PR on Windows, write the body to a temp file and use gh pr create -F <file> — a bash heredoc and a PowerShell @'...'@ here-string both fail for gh pr create --body (here-strings work for git commit -m, not PR bodies). Move .agent-work/commander-315/ to .agent-work/archive/<date>-commander-315/. Run the archive-phase capture gate before marking archive complete — it additionally requires git to TRACK the episode, which is what proves the record outlived this worktree: py /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/verify_episode_captured.py commander-315 --store-root episodes --phase archive. Confirm the branch is clean and merge-ready per repo guidance. The engine mechanically refuses closeout (c4) when the staged diff includes suspicious artifacts (oversized files, generated record dumps, disallowed dirs, binary/blob additions, large data files); if any are intentional, a human waives c4 via <engine> waive archive --cond c4 --authority human --reason "..." rather than hand-editing the spine. Release the engine session lease only as your VERY LAST action, AFTER the archive postconditions pass and you have run the engine's final advance on archive (the advance that marks the spine done): by default call the spine_lease MCP tool with action=release (this is your own spine; the door needs no session id argument). CLI fallback: <engine> release --session-id commander-commander-315. Release must come after that closing advance, never before it — the lease must cover every journaled action, so the release is the final journal entry; releasing earlier leaves archive's own closeout entries (attest/waive/advance) after the lease release and fails the terminal provenance check.

postconditions.statement: work area archived and this run's episode captured AND tracked by git, so the record survives this worktree

the work is REACHABLE: this branch has a pull request that is OPEN or MERGED. A merged PR is reachable work; a closed-unmerged one is not, and neither is no PR at all. A terminal spine and a pushed branch describe the run, not the ref -- CI never runs on an unopened branch, and every commander that reached a terminal spine without opening one had to be chased for it. Open the PR even if the work is unfinished; declare FINAL or PENDING in its title and hand the merge up. Two properties of the check text are load-bearing. The branch is derived at CHECK time from the repo root, never resolved at instantiation: init instantiates the spine before it starts the branch, so the branch need not exist yet -- and a literal branch placeholder is not a resolver-owned token, so instantiation cannot catch one and would ship it unsubstituted. The count is compared in the SHELL because the engine's verdict for a command condition is the EXIT CODE and stdout is discarded: gh --jq 'length > 0' prints true or false but exits 0 either way, so that form can never fail.

check.command: test "$(gh pr list --head "$(git -C /home/tommy/projects/constellation-skills-wt/epic-568-315 rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" --state all --json state --jq '[.[] | select(.state == "OPEN" or .state == "MERGED")] | length')" -gt 0

triage_candidates.statement: Identity checks need an explicit engine contract. verify_worktree_isolation.py --here reads the ambient cwd as the SUBJECT of the check, not as a path base, so any engine change that relocates a command check's cwd makes it tautological. Needs a schema flag or a launcher-cwd env var passed into the check environment. Engine-core architecture change; floated.

11 of 22 shipped command checks are cwd-dependent only because they invoke a script whose --root defaults to cwd (init_work_area.py, verify_state_note.py, verify_cycles.py, verify_spec_confirmed.py, verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py). Pinning those roots in the templates would remove the dependence at the authoring side regardless of what the engine does.

checklist_engine.py main() does not resolve the --file path, so base_dir = path.parent is relative whenever --file is. Any base_dir-derived path walk no-ops on the CLI form every crew member is told to use.

generate_spine.py emits every command anchored cd <repo-root> and 394 checked-in checks already carry that prefix, so a shell cd would override an engine-set cwd. Whether the generator keeps emitting the prefix is an open decision that any cwd fix must settle.

Three different cwd rules coexist inside one _check_condition dispatch: command checks inherit the launcher cwd, git-change-policy uses base_dir, and load_config resolves config_ref against Path.cwd() first. load_config decides rework_cap and the trip band, so a spine driven from elsewhere loads its rigor config from a stranger's directory.

docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md lines 39-41 and scripts/init_work_area.py lines 129-134 both state the no-cwd behaviour as present fact and cite issue 341 as the tracking issue. No test asserts either, so they will silently go stale the day a cwd fix lands.

why_trail.why: Project overlay read (docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md, CREW_CONTEXT.md, GLOSSARY.md); map is DEGRADED-UNPARSEABLE and discharged with three hash-pinned substitutes. The load-bearing substitute is docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md:39-41, which already records this exact defect and names the repo root as the anchor the corpus assumes.

Defect reproduces live on both halves: a decoy file in the launcher's cwd ADVANCED gate gA (fail-open, as filed), and the project's own file was invisible to gate gB (false-red, not filed). base_dir is already threaded to _check_condition and consumed by the git-change-policy branch; only the command branch drops it. Enumeration settles what cwd must resolve to: zero shipped checks are spine-dir-relative, all 17 cwd-dependent ones are repo-root-relative, so cwd = the repo root enclosing the spine repairs all of them and requires zero template edits.
